intro:
Use it to show when something was busy, across many days: commits, spending, requests per hour. Each column is a period, usually a week, and each row a bin inside it, usually a day. The shade carries the count.

It does not suit reading exact values. Use it to find where to look, and the tooltip or a [Bar Chart](/docs/web/charts/bar-chart) to say how much.

parts.Header: The strip above the grid: `title`, `value` and `caption`, with the ramp or your own control on the trailing side.
parts.XAxis: Month labels above the grid, one where the month changes. `labels` puts your own over each column.
parts.YAxis: Weekday labels beside the grid. The grid is sized around its `width`.
parts.Separator: Vertical rules that group the columns, behind the cells.
parts.Cells: The grid. Without this part no cells are drawn.
parts.Tooltip: Makes the grid readable by pointer and keyboard, and shows a line for the cell being read.
parts.Legend: The key under the grid: `lessLabel`, the five steps of the ramp, `moreLabel`.

examples.title: Scrolling a full year
examples.description: The default `layout` is `fluid`, which draws cells at `binSize` and is as wide as that needs. Put the chart in a horizontal scroller. A `legend` on the header stays above the grid, and `HeatmapChart.Separator` marks the quarters.

examples.title: Week start, language and labels
examples.description: Pass the same `weekStartDay` to `buildHeatmapCalendar` and to the chart. `formatLabel` on the x-axis, `labels` on the y-axis, and `lessLabel` and `moreLabel` on the legend take your own strings. `Tooltip.formatLabel` also receives the cells outside the range, which have no date. `formatCellLabel` is what a screen reader says for each day, and returning nothing leaves that day out.

examples.title: Changing the colour
examples.description: `color` swaps the base of the ramp and `emptyColor` the empty cell. Each takes a theme role, a token by name such as `--chart-3`, or any CSS colour. `levelColors` replaces all five colours, and `levelOpacity` retunes the contrast.

examples.title: A grid whose bins are not days
examples.description: Build `data` yourself, without dates, and pass `labels` to both axes. Set `rows` when there are not seven of them. Add `formatLabel` on the tooltip to name what a cell counts.

examples.title: Reading the cell above the chart
examples.description: `onActiveCellChange` reports the cell being read, and `null` when there is none, for a readout outside the chart or in its header. `inactiveOpacity` dims the others. A `formatLabel` that returns an empty string hides the line beside the cell.

notes:
### Sizing

A `fluid` chart is as wide as its cells need, and its height always follows from the cell size and `rows`. A `fill` chart fits its container's width, so a long range makes small cells. Cells narrower than about 6 pixels are hard to point at. For those, use `fluid` in a scroller.

### The ramp

The levels come from the quartiles of the non-zero counts, so small and large numbers both use the whole ramp. Pass `levels` to fix the thresholds, for instance to compare two charts on one scale.

### Reading

A mouse reads the cell under it. A click or a tap pins the reading, and pressing the same cell again clears it. A swipe does not read a cell, so a scroller around the chart still scrolls. Once the grid has focus, the arrow keys walk it, Home and End go to the ends of a row, and Escape clears the reading. All of this comes from `HeatmapChart.Tooltip`.

### Accessibility

The chart renders a list of its days for a screen reader, and announces the cell being read. The default label is a count of contributions and a date, so pass `formatCellLabel` when the cells count something else, and `label` to name the chart. A year is a long list, so return nothing from `formatCellLabel` for days that have nothing to say.

With reduced motion set, or `animationDuration={0}`, the grid draws at once with no reveal.

### Building the weeks

`buildHeatmapCalendar` turns dated counts into `weeks`. It comes from the chart's client entry, so a Server Component cannot call it. Call it in a client file, and pass dates and counts from the server as props.
propsNote: `HeatmapChart`, `HeatmapChart.Header`, `HeatmapChart.XAxis`, `HeatmapChart.YAxis` and `HeatmapChart.Legend` also take the props of the element they render, and a `className`. `HeatmapChart.Tooltip` puts its `className` on the readout. The other parts draw nothing themselves and take only the props listed.
